internalId: 583d9c88-b71c-4560-92ad-3e23d33bf1d0
---

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

# App Style Guide â€” Kanban / MDÂ² (React + MUI)

How to build **any new component** so it matches the app. This is written for **Material UI v5+** components.

**The theme is the source of truth.** All color, radius, base typography, and spacing units live in the single `createTheme` (defined in `GUIDANCE.md` Â§1/Â§9). This guide does **not** define colors â€” it tells you **which theme value to use for which role**, and covers the things the theme can't encode: layout, spacing/margins, borders, elevation, and component conventions.

**The one rule that matters:** never write a raw hex, px radius, or magic color into a component. Read it from the theme (`theme.palette.*`, `theme.shape`, `theme.typography`, `theme.spacing`). If a component has a hardcoded hex in its `sx`/styled, it's wrong â€” that's exactly where the look drifts and where dark mode breaks.

---

## 1. How to consume the theme

- **Colors:** `sx={{ color: 'text.secondary', bgcolor: 'background.paper', borderColor: 'divider' }}` â€” MUI resolves dotted palette paths automatically in `sx`. In `styled`/JS use the callback form: `styled(Box)(({ theme }) => ({ color: theme.palette.text.secondary }))`.
- **Spacing:** use the 8px unit via the spacing scale â€” `sx={{ p: 2, gap: 1, mt: 1.5 }}` (`2` = 16px, `1` = 8px). Don't write `padding: '16px'`.
- **Radius:** `borderRadius: 1` (= `theme.shape.borderRadius` = 8) and multiples; for the fixed non-8 radii see Â§4.
- **Typography:** prefer `Typography variant=...` and `theme.typography.*` over ad-hoc `fontSize`.
- **Custom tokens:** roles the default MUI palette doesn't cover (column/track surfaces, the strong/hover border steps, `text-3/4`, section-header color, `primary-bg` tint, status colors) must exist in the theme under a namespace (e.g. `theme.palette.custom.*`) with light + dark values. Consume them the same way â€” `bgcolor: 'custom.column'`. **Never inline their hex.** If a needed token doesn't exist yet, add it to the theme, don't hardcode it in the component.

---

## 2. Role â†’ theme slot

Pick the slot by the element's **role**, not by how it looks in one mode:

| Role | Theme slot |
|---|---|
| App background; tinted footer/action bars | `background.default` |
| Column & sidebar surface | `custom.column` |
| Segmented-control / toolbar track, hover fill | `custom.track` |
| Card, dialog, popup, input surface | `background.paper` |
| Hairlines, resting borders | `divider` |
| Input borders, vertical separators | `custom.borderStrong` |
| Border on hover | `custom.borderHover` |
| Titles, values, headings | `text.primary` |
| Body copy, field labels | `text.secondary` |
| Meta, captions, resting icons | `custom.text3` |
| Muted / placeholder / disabled | `custom.text4` |
| Uppercase section/column headers | `custom.colHead` |
| The one CTA, selection, focus, links, icon-hover | `primary.main` |
| Contained-button hover | `primary.dark` |
| Selected/tinted bg, focus ring, ID-chip bg | `custom.primaryBg` |
| Text/icon on a primary fill | `primary.contrastText` |
| Active / saved / online dot | `success.main` |
| Destructive action | `error.main` |
| Status swatch dots & ID-chip tints (decorative only) | `custom.status.*` |

Rules: **one** `primary` per surface (the CTA/selection accent) â€” everything else is `text-*`/`divider`. Status colors are **decoration only** (dots, chip tints), never interactive color. Dark-mode brightness/tinting is handled inside the theme's two palettes, so a correctly-sloted component needs zero per-mode code.

---

## 3. Layout

- **Full-height app:** column flex â€” menu row / ribbon / content (`flex: 1; minHeight: 0`) / status bar. Fixed bands `flexShrink: 0`.
- **Board:** horizontal-scroll flex row, `gap: 2` (16px), page padding `p: 2.5` (20px); columns `width: 296, flexShrink: 0`, internal column flex `gap: 1`.

While in diagram-view mode, editing a mind map, I have a node selected, then want to use the + sign next to the breadcrumbs -bar, but this is disabled. don't know why. 

I believe it should be possible to add sub diagrams also from mind maps.

## Current state

The breadcrumb **Add child diagram** button observes only the selected item in the saved Current diagram. Editing uses `DiagramSelectionService`, which owns a separate selection for the editable New diagram. Selecting an editable node therefore does not enable the button. This affects every editable diagram type, not only mind maps.

Child diagrams are indexed by a persisted parent diagram ID and item ID. A newly added editable item cannot be a child-diagram parent until the edited copy containing it has been saved and opened.

## Implementation details

* Pass `DiagramSelectionService` to `DiagramBreadcrumbBar` and subscribe to its selection with `useSyncExternalStore` while the active diagram is being edited.
* When the editor selection is non-empty, enable the button only when exactly one selected node or connection has the same ID and kind in the saved Current diagram. Resolve its label from Current so the child context matches its persisted parent. A group, multiple selection, or newly added item remains ineligible.
* When the editor selection is empty, retain the existing Current-selection behavior.
* Open the child action through `DiagramViewService` with the resolved persisted parent. The service must validate that the diagram is active and that the item still exists before creating the child context. Do not copy editor selection into the service's Current selection state.
* Update the breadcrumb and view-service tests. Cover an existing editable mind-map node, another diagram type, Current-selection fallback, multiple selection, group selection, a newly added item, and a stale or missing persisted item.

## Acceptance criteria

* Selecting one existing node in an editable mind map enables **Add child diagram** and opens a child action for that node in the active persisted diagram.
* The same behavior works for one existing node or connection in every supported editable diagram type.
* With no editor selection, a valid Current selection continues to enable the button and open the child action.
* The button is disabled when the editor selection contains multiple objects, a group, or an item that does not exist in Current.
* A newly added editable item cannot receive a child diagram until the edited copy containing it is saved and opened.
* The child action uses the persisted parent diagram ID, item ID, and Current item label.

We should remove this and instead use the default save button on the 'home' tab. When a user edits the diagram, it should, like all other cards and actions and such be saved automatically through the [commit_batcher.ts](app/src/data/commit_batcher.ts)

## Current state

During diagram editing, the Diagram tab shows a separate `DiagramSaveButton`. It calls `DiagramSaveService.save()`, which queues current edited diagram copy and diagram index, then immediately flushes shared commit batch.

Diagram edits already enter normal persistence automatically. `DiagramSaveService` subscribes to model mutations, serializes canonical diagram data, and asks `DiagramViewService` to queue diagram copy and index changes. `DataService.scheduleDiagramCommit()` sends them to `CommitBatcher`, which commits after configured automatic delay. Home-tab Commit button and `Ctrl+S` also flush same pending batch through `ProjectPersistenceService`.

`DiagramSaveService.save()` has two other workflow uses: Review dialog saves before closing, and New diagram creation saves dirty current diagram before switching. Those uses protect workflow transitions and are not duplicate toolbar controls.

## Implementation details

* Remove `DiagramSaveButton` from `DiagramMenuTab`, then remove unused button component and its focused component test.
* Update `DiagramMenuTab` tests to require edit, clipboard, review, metadata, legend, formatting, and comparison controls without a diagram-specific Save/Saved button.
* Keep automatic model-mutation subscription and existing persistence chain: `DiagramSaveService` queues canonical diagram copy plus diagram index through `DiagramViewService`, `DataService`, and `CommitBatcher`. Do not add direct file writes or another diagram persistence path.
* Keep `DiagramSaveService.save()` for Review and New diagram transition workflows. Those operations still require an immediate flush before their next step.
* Keep Home-tab Commit button and `Ctrl+S` as manual immediate-flush entry points. Automatic `CommitBatcher` timer remains normal background persistence path.
* Preserve failure behavior. Queue failures use diagram error dialog; commit failures remain pending, keep edit session dirty, and use project persistence error reporting.
* Retain service tests proving model mutation queues without explicit Save and acknowledgement occurs only after persistence. Add or adjust menu and project-persistence coverage proving diagram changes enable and flush through shared Commit action.

## Acceptance criteria

* Diagram tab contains no diagram-specific Save or Saved control before, during, or after an edit.
* Editing diagram automatically queues canonical diagram copy and diagram index in shared `CommitBatcher`; user does not need to open Home tab or press Save first.
* Queued diagram changes make shared project persistence dirty, enable Home-tab Commit action, and can be flushed with Home Commit or `Ctrl+S`.
* If user takes no manual action, configured automatic commit delay flushes queued diagram and index changes through normal batch flow.
* Successful persistence acknowledges saved copy and clears diagram dirty state only for data included in that commit. Edits made during persistence remain dirty and queue again.
* Commit failure leaves diagram changes pending and editable, with existing user-visible error reporting.
* Review dialog Save and dirty-diagram handling before New diagram creation still complete immediate persistence before closing or switching diagrams.
* Cards, actions, other files, diagram Review behavior, diagram creation, commit batching, push behavior, and read-only behavior remain unchanged.

Yes. It currently mixes four responsibilities: list layout, sorting, entry formatting, and entry rendering. I’d split it into three focused units—not more.

### Recommended structure

1. `action_run_history.tsx`
   - Owns the “Run history” section layout.
   - Reports `error` through `dialogService`.
   - Reads configured agent accounts once.
   - Renders the ordered entries.

2. `action_run_history_entry.tsx`
   - Owns one history entry.
   - Builds agent/command summaries.
   - Resolves persisted account IDs to current account names.
   - Renders associated `CommitReferenceRow` components.

3. `action_run_history_order.ts`
   - Exports `newestFirstHistoryEntries`.
   - Encapsulates the stable newest-first ordering.
   - Returns the entry plus its source index, as it does today.

This would reduce [action_run_history.tsx](C:\Users\janbo\Documents\dev\md2\app\src\components\actions\run\state\action_run_history.tsx) to roughly 45 lines and give the non-React ordering logic an independent test boundary.

### Suggested ownership

```text
ActionRunHistoryOwner
  └─ loads/subscribes to ActionHistoryStore
      └─ ActionRunHistory
          ├─ reports load errors
          ├─ orders entries
          └─ HistoryEntry
              ├─ formats its summary
              └─ renders commit references
```

I would keep summary construction inside `action_run_history_entry.tsx`. Extracting tiny helpers such as `formatCompletedAt`, `resolveAccountName`, and `agentConfiguration` into separate files would fragment straightforward presentation logic without creating a meaningful reusable unit.

### Test split

- `action_run_history.test.tsx`
  - Empty history.
  - Error reporting.
  - Section rendering.

- `action_run_history_entry.test.tsx`
  - Agent configuration and account-name rendering.
  - Command output rendering.
  - Commit rows and diff interaction.

- `action_run_history_order.node.test.ts`
  - Newest-first order.
  - Tie-breaking.
  - Source array remains unchanged.

### Other cleanup worth including

- Make semicolon usage consistent with the project style.
- Reorder imports consistently.
- Destructure component arguments directly where it improves clarity.
- Preserve the account lookup in the list boundary so every row does not independently subscribe to configuration.
- Preserve the source index for tie-breaking, but recognize it is not durable React identity. The domain type has no run ID, so there is currently no genuinely stable key. I would not invent one during this refactor.
- Keep error reporting in an effect. It correctly avoids throwing or mutating state during rendering.
- Do not move sorting into `ActionHistoryStore`: newest-first order is presentation policy, while the store should retain the loaded model data.

So: yes, splitting is worthwhile, but the clean boundary is three files rather than breaking every formatter into its own helper. No files have been changed.

we currently have a lot of components that wrap another component, have the same name as the componet they wrap with '\_owner' appended and just wrap those components in order to pass a prop into them.

This is the wrong architectural approach. we don't want to use this. The idea comes from an instruction that those components need to be self contained: a change in the property should not trigger a render in the parent. Meaning, these should never have been properties. Updates to these properties come from events and this should be handled within the component.

So we need to refactor and remove all those \_owner versions, put the value updates inside the components, remove the properties and replace the '\_owner' versions with the proper components.

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

This is very strange behavior, nothing changed on the action, yet is still reloads multiple times.
* same thing after closing or opening a card: totally unrelated action popups reload. this is not correct behavior, as nothing about the action popups has changed, no data it relies on has changed.

## Current state

`ActionPromptOwner` owns prompt preparation, draft selection, attachments, scheduling, execution, phrases, and controls, while `ActionAgentPrompt` receives the resulting data and JSX. This separates the feature behavior from the component that should own it and makes `responsePrompts` and `bottomRow` feature-specific JSX properties.

The stores passed through the popup component tree are not global service references. `createActionPopupBindings()` creates `bindingStore`, `conversationStore`, `historyStore`, `inputStore`, `resultStore`, `scheduleStore`, and the layout stores for one selected action and context. `settingsStore` is also a scoped card/action or session/action store returned by a global service. Passing every scoped store separately exposes runtime wiring and creates large forwarding interfaces. The assignment and base contexts are scoped values rather than services; different open popups can have different contexts.

`ActionPopup` subscribes to the complete project state through `useProjectState()`. Any project snapshot replacement therefore rerenders the popup tree, including changes to unrelated cards. Several prompt consumers also subscribe to complete store snapshots while using only one or two fields.

Subscribe separately to the current project reference and the target card fields actually used by the popup: identity, title, worktree assignment, and conversation/activity references. Resolve card subscriptions by `cardInternalId`; paths remain persistence locations and must not become popup identity.
8. Read persisted action state only when selecting the initial action. Do not retain a project-snapshot subscription for that initialization value. Subscribe to historical activity only for historical contexts.

Replace complete prompt-store snapshots with stable projections for the values that affect prompt rendering: run status, active action type, interaction readiness, question identity, selected conversation, conversation loading state, and conversion message. Event handlers must read current values directly when a value does not affect rendering.

Let the prompt use the remaining height, with the markdown editor flexing while phrase buttons and the bottom row remain fixed. Keep the existing persisted, explicitly resized layout behavior.
12. Publish a layout snapshot only when a layout value changes. A question update may cause one render for the relevant run projection and one additional render only when measurement changes the layout snapshot.

## Acceptance criteria

* `ActionPromptOwner` and its file are removed, and both agent and command flows render `ActionAgentPrompt` directly.
* `ActionAgentPrompt` owns the complete prompt feature and has no `ReactNode`, `responsePrompts`, or `bottomRow` properties.
* `ActionAgentPrompt` receives one `ActionPopupRuntime` instead of separate properties for every runtime store, and no intermediate component forwards those stores individually.
* Two open popups retain separate runtime-store instances and cannot observe or mutate each other's prompt, conversation, history, schedule, result, binding, or layout state.
* Assignment and base contexts remain explicit scoped values and retain `cardInternalId` as canonical card identity.
* Editing, opening, or closing an unrelated card does not render `ActionPopupContent`, `ActionAgentPrompt`, the prompt editor, phrase buttons, or bottom controls in an already open popup.
* Replacing a project snapshot without changing a popup dependency does not reconfigure the popup session or recreate its runtime stores.
* Changing the target card title updates only the target display. Changing its worktree updates only worktree-dependent UI. Changing its conversation/activity references updates only conversation or historical-activity consumers.
* Closed schedule UI does not render because another card changes.
* When questions fit below `questionsMaxHeight`, the questions region uses its content height and the prompt fills the remaining space.
* When questions exceed `questionsMaxHeight`, the questions region is capped and scrolls; the prompt remains at least `promptMinHeight`.
* The markdown editor fills the prompt space not used by phrase buttons and the bottom controls.
* A question update causes no more than one prompt render from run state and one additional render when the measured layout snapshot changes, excluding development `StrictMode` duplication.
* Existing prompt resizing, restored questions, command input, scheduling, phrase insertion, attachments, and keyboard-run behavior continue to work.
* Focused popup and prompt tests pass, including regression tests for unrelated project changes and question layout.
